description:
The Community Based Training Scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2016.

This scheme is part of the larger initiative to enhance the skill development of marginalized communities.

The primary objective of the Community Based Training Scheme is to provide skill training to individuals from economically weaker sections of society.

The scheme aims to empower these individuals by improving their employability and self-employment opportunities.

It specifically targets youth aged between 15 to 35 years.

The scheme focuses on providing training in various sectors such as agriculture, manufacturing, services, and entrepreneurship.

The training is designed to be community-driven and is implemented through local organizations.

The scheme emphasizes the importance of local needs and market demands in determining the training programs.

The Community Based Training Scheme aims to train approximately 1 million individuals by the end of 2025.

The training duration varies from 3 months to 12 months depending on the skill being taught.

Participants are provided with a stipend during their training period to support their livelihood.

The stipend amount is set at INR 2,000 per month for the duration of the training.

The scheme also encourages the involvement of local industries to ensure that the training is relevant to the job market.

The training programs are designed to be flexible and can be adapted to the specific needs of the community.

Eligible organizations for implementing the scheme include non-governmental organizations, community-based organizations, and local self-governments.

These organizations must have experience in skill development and community mobilization.

To apply for the scheme, organizations must submit a detailed project proposal to the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.

The proposal should outline the training programs, target beneficiaries, and expected outcomes.

The application process requires the submission of documents such as the organization's registration certificate, PAN card, and previous project reports.

Once the proposal is approved, the implementing organization can begin conducting training sessions.

The scheme is funded by the Government of India, which allocates a budget specifically for skill development initiatives.

In the financial year 2021-2022, the budget allocation for skill development was INR 3,000 crores.

The Community Based Training Scheme is monitored by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.

Regular audits and evaluations are conducted to assess the effectiveness of the training programs.

The scheme also includes a provision for post-training support to help participants secure employment or start their own businesses.

This support may include access to financial assistance, mentorship, and networking opportunities.

The Community Based Training Scheme aligns with the National Skill Development Mission.

The National Skill Development Mission was launched in 2015 with the goal of enhancing the skill sets of the Indian workforce.

The mission aims to create a skilled workforce of 500 million by 2022.

The Community Based Training Scheme contributes to this mission by focusing on community-based training and local needs.

The scheme also plays a crucial role in promoting entrepreneurship among youth.

By providing skill training and support, the scheme aims to reduce unemployment rates in rural and urban areas.

The implementation of the scheme is carried out at the state level by the respective State Skill Development Missions.

These missions are responsible for coordinating training programs and ensuring quality standards.

The scheme has seen participation from various stakeholders including government bodies, private sector organizations, and civil society.

The Community Based Training Scheme has been instrumental in bridging the skill gap in various sectors.

It has also contributed to the overall economic development of communities by enhancing productivity.

The scheme has a strong focus on women empowerment by encouraging female participation in skill training.

Special provisions are made for women and marginalized groups to ensure their inclusion in the training programs.

The scheme has reported a significant increase in the number of trained individuals since its inception.

As of 2023, over 500,000 individuals have successfully completed training under this scheme.

The success stories of trained individuals highlight the positive impact of the scheme on their livelihoods.

Many participants have reported increased income levels and improved quality of life after completing their training.

The Community Based Training Scheme is a vital component of India's broader strategy to achieve sustainable development goals.

It emphasizes the importance of skill development in reducing poverty and enhancing social equity.

The scheme is also aligned with the Make in India initiative, which aims to boost manufacturing and job creation.

The Community Based Training Scheme continues to evolve based on feedback from participants and stakeholders.

The Government of India is committed to expanding the reach and effectiveness of the scheme.

Future plans include increasing the budget allocation and expanding the range of skills offered.

The scheme is expected to play a crucial role in post-pandemic recovery by providing training to those affected by job losses.

Overall, the Community Based Training Scheme represents a significant effort by the Government of India to empower communities through skill development.

It provides a structured approach to training that is responsive to local needs and market demands.

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to fostering inclusive growth and development in the country.
